title: Fake IDs, dual lives & a dramatic escape: The 28-yr saga of killer Rajinder Bairagi
content: The Delhi Police successfully arrested Rajinder Bairagi, a long-sought fugitive connected to a 1998 murder case. For nearly thirty years, he managed to evade law enforcement by living under a false identity in Madhya Pradesh. During the investigation, authorities also resolved two previously unsolved attempted murder cases from 1997 using leads tied to him. His elaborate disguise was ultimately dismantled following comprehensive surveillance operations.

title: If asked whom to believe, I’ll say Gen Z: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat
content: Mohan Bhagwat advocated for system correction through protests and increased education budgets. He opposed social media bans and favored dialogue with Pakistan and China. Traditional family structures should be upheld while creating space for same-sex relationships. Bhagwat explained women's independence from the RSS apex decision-making body. Societal disrespect for manual labor causes competition for government jobs, he stated.

title: India's search for answers to rediscover lost glory in Tests begins in Colombo
content: India begin their three-day warm-up fixture against Sri Lanka XI at the NCC in Colombo today. The Shubman Gill-led unit has already had two intense training sessions and a largely rested squad means the team feels fresh for the crucial series starting August 15. There are some injury concerns: Jasprit Bumrah, Washington Sundar, and Sai Sudharsan. However, the squad has enough quality to secure a scoreline that keeps their World Test Championship final chances alive.

title: Oil prices rise 1% as Middle East conflict continues Hormuz shipping disruption
content: On Friday, oil prices experienced a modest rise amid shipping uncertainties in the Strait of Hormuz. Traders exhibit caution regarding transit through this critical route. Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump hinted at a potential resolution to the ongoing conflict. Additionally, Iran and Oman are exploring new transit options for the waterway. As developments unfolded, market trends reversed previous declines.

title: Zohran Mamdani tells Amazon, Walmart and 40 others: Stop selling these devices
content: In a bold move to safeguard the community, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has mandated that online retailers cease the sale of illegal high-speed e-bikes, aiming to improve public safety and reduce tragic incidents. Additionally, the mayor has suggested launching five city-funded grocery stores throughout the city, which would provide essential goods at significantly reduced prices, ensuring that average New Yorkers benefit from substantial savings each year.

title: 'I was India's 12th man for two years': Ajinkya Rahane reveals
content: Ajinkya Rahane, who recently announced his retirement from all forms of cricket, scored 5,077 runs in 85 Tests at an average of 38.46, including 12 centuries and 26 half-centuries. He also played 90 ODIs, scoring 2962 runs at an average of 35.26, including 3 hundreds and 24 fifties. He also featured in 20 T20Is for India.

title: Priscilla Chan founded a school in 2016; 10 yrs later, it closed after $125m funding
content: After ten years of service, The Primary School, co-founded by Priscilla Chan, will conclude its operations in June. This institution, known for offering tuition-free education and extensive family support, struggled to achieve state-average academic results despite receiving generous funding from the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative. The Initiative has decided to redirect its philanthropic priorities towards funding scientific research instead.

title: Hawaii candidate Kirill Basin charged, held on $1M bail after Maui beach clash
content: At Keawakapu Beach, Democratic congressional hopeful Kirill Basin encountered serious legal issues after reportedly threatening individuals with a knife and a gun. A bystander, trained in martial arts, bravely intervened and rendered Basin unconscious during the altercation. Now charged with terroristic threatening, Basin faces a one million dollar bail, further complicated by a troubling history of previous arrests for assault and property damage.

title: Influencer Sydney Towle dies at 26 after rare cancer battle
content: Content creator Sydney Towle, who inspired millions by documenting her battle with a rare form of cancer, has died at the age of 26. In the days following her death, an emotional clip from a 2025 podcast interview has resurfaced online, with many calling it a powerful reminder of the legacy she leaves behind. Sydney's brother Austin Towle recalled her final days.

title: Kevin O'Leary: Wall Street boom may not shape 2026 elections
content: Canadian billionaire Kevin O'Leary notes a disconnect between strong US economic indicators and household affordability struggles. He believes energy costs, particularly gasoline prices, will significantly influence upcoming elections. O'Leary also predicts increased North American economic integration driven by China's growing global influence. Canada offers energy and minerals, the US provides scale and innovation, and Mexico is vital. This cooperation is seen as an economic necessity amid global technological races.

title: Rahul Gandhi ignored offer to end my fast, says Sonam Wangchuk
content: Sonam Wangchuk voiced disappointment with political leaders after his hunger strike concluded. His wife Gitanjali sought Rahul Gandhi's involvement but received no positive response. Union ministers also reportedly broke a promise regarding the release of photos. Wangchuk felt leaders showed a narrow approach and arrived late to his protest. He praised the apolitical CJP organization for its fair and just advocacy.

title: Aryna Sabalenka, Jessica Pegula back WTA’s new gender testing rule
content: In a significant move, the WTA has enacted a new policy requiring all players to undergo a one-time SRY gene test for eligibility. Aryna Sabalenka, currently the top-ranked player, champions this measure as a means of ensuring fairness in the sport. However, Jessica Pegula, a member of the players' council, perceives it as a bureaucratic tweak with little resistance, reflecting a range of sentiments among players regarding the policy.

title: NBA trade rumor: Heat eye $48M Pistons star to help Giannis Antetokounmpo
content: Miami Heat are reportedly exploring a trade to reunite with sharpshooter Duncan Robinson, sending Nikola Jovic and two second-round picks to Detroit in return. The move would pair Robinson's 41 percent three-point shooting with Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo, addressing a spacing gap left after Miami's offseason moves. Robinson's $15.99 million cap hit lines up closely with Jovic's, making the framework financially realistic for both sides.

title: UPI charges: Lok Sabha passes Bill for government to make changes
content: The Lok Sabha has taken a vital step by passing a Bill aimed at simplifying tax rules to enhance investment attractiveness. The new legislation abolishes a limitation on specific electronic payment options, allowing banks and providers to charge merchants on transactions. Additionally, the government is empowered to revise the zero-MDR scheme for UPI and RuPay. This initiative is poised to drive advancements in the financial sector’s infrastructure and innovative capabilities.

title: SC dismisses plea challenging Delhi HC relief to Hinduja brothers in Bofors case
content: The Supreme Court has officially closed the chapter on the Bofors payoff case by dismissing an appeal that challenged the Delhi high court's 2005 ruling, which had previously annulled criminal proceedings against the Hinduja brothers. Advocate Ajay K Agrawal filed the appeal, but the court decided against allowing more time for arguments, finalizing the legal dispute once and for all.

title: Rain threat looms large over IND vs SL three-day warm-up match
content: India's preparations for the two-Test series against Sri Lanka could be affected by rain, with wet weather forecast in Colombo during the three-day warm-up match against Sri Lanka XI. Heavy showers are expected from Friday morning to Sunday afternoon, raising doubts over how much playing time both teams will get before the first Test in Galle.

title: Netanyahu calls PM Modi, discusses bilateral ties, West Asia situation
content: In a significant phone discussion, Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu evaluated the progress made in their strategic partnership and bilateral engagements. They also addressed current developments in West Asia, amidst Israel's increasing international scrutiny due to its military actions. This exchange highlights their continued efforts to bolster cooperation and deepen ties between India and Israel.

title: 'It will end pretty soon': Trump hints at early resolution to US-Iran war
content: Expressing confidence, US President Trump suggested that the Iran conflict is nearing its end, arguing that Tehran cannot bear its continuation. He remains hopeful about negotiations related to the Strait of Hormuz. The US is resolute in preventing Iran from developing nuclear weapons. Meanwhile, Iran's defence minister asserts that their military is on standby for any potential threats, and the parliament speaker claims that the US.

title: Jana Nayagan day 15: Thalapathy Vijay film grosses Rs 308.67 crore worldwide
content: Jana Nayagan's box office collections saw a decline on its fifteenth day. The film has now surpassed Rs 300 crore in worldwide gross collections. Its India net collection reached Rs 185.15 crore after fifteen days. Tamil Nadu remained the strongest market, contributing significantly to daily earnings. The movie's performance reflects Vijay's enduring star power.

title: Rahane snubs MS Dhoni, Virat Kohli; names India's greatest-ever cricketer
content: Ajinkya Rahane recently retired from all cricket formats. He named Sachin Tendulkar as India's greatest-ever cricketer. Tendulkar had a remarkable 24-year international career for India. Rahane played alongside Tendulkar in domestic and IPL matches. He also captained India in all three formats.

title: Devendra Fadnavis roots for 'Ramayana' winning an Oscar
content: In a show of support, Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis has championed Nitesh Tiwari's upcoming film 'Ramayana'. He expressed optimism that this mythological masterpiece will capture an Oscar, citing its impressive scale and production quality. The initial installment is slated for release in November 2026, with the date officially confirmed by Sony Pictures. Read on to know more in detail.

title: Alternative-fuel passenger vehicles fast catching up with petrol ones
content: In a significant shift, alternative-fuel passenger vehicles have captured forty percent of the retail market, nearly matching petrol-powered models, which hold a slender one percent lead. July marked the highest sales figures for automobiles ever recorded. Additionally, electric two-wheelers are experiencing unprecedented market penetration, highlighting changing consumer preferences towards cost-effective options.

title: Survey reveals about 81% of study-abroad aspirants plan to return home
content: Nearly all Indian students heading overseas for education plan to come back home after their studies. What's striking is that about 90% are pioneering this journey as the first in their families to study abroad. This trend highlights a shift towards self-driven decisions among students. Business and management fields are particularly appealing, with many utilizing Google searches and agents to find their perfect educational fit.

title: Temporary disability certificate won't deny MBBS seat for students PwBD quota: NMC
content: Candidates holding temporary disability certificates can now pursue MBBS admissions, reflecting significant changes in the National Medical Commission's policies. The revised guidelines indicate that admission requests from persons with disabilities will be subject to assessment by medical boards. It is noteworthy that the presence of progressive or non-progressive disabilities will not inherently prevent admission, with a thorough evaluation of functional competency taking place.

title: Kharge-Rijiju face-off in Rajya Sabha; opposition stalls House over Amit Shah
content: The Rajya Sabha approved the Appropriation Bill, 2026, authorizing fund withdrawals for excess expenditure. Opposition members repeatedly demanded Home Minister Amit Shah's presence in the House.  Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju was asked to convey their sentiments to Shah.  Leader of the Opposition Mallikarjun Kharge sought the Home Minister's statement on student police action.  The opposition also requested the Prime Minister's apology for the alleged police excesses.

title: Settling with a few cases won't stop CBI probe: Supreme Court warns realtors
content: The Supreme Court will continue CBI investigations into defaulting realtors. Builders cannot escape probes by settling with only a few homebuyers. Many bank officials are found to have colluded with these builders. CBI has completed probes in eighteen of fifty registered cases. Banks must grant prosecution sanctions for accused officials within two weeks.

title: ‘Michael 2’ under way, film makers to start shooting by 2026 end
content: Filming for the Michael Jackson biopic sequel is slated to begin by year's end.  The production company aims for a potential 2027 release date for the film.  This sequel follows the significant worldwide success of the first movie.  Some omitted elements from the initial film may appear in the new installment.  The company reported overall financial gains due to recent film successes.

title: UP polls: Congress MPs urge leadership to seal SP alliance deal early
content: Uttar Pradesh Congress MPs are actively pushing for a partnership with the Samajwadi Party, considering it vital to mount a formidable challenge to the BJP in the upcoming elections. With a strong consensus among the MPs for quick action, party leaders are currently assessing viable constituencies and gathering data to facilitate negotiations, striving to strengthen their united front against the BJP's dominance in the state.

title: Can't exclude SC/ST creamy layer from quotas: Government to Supreme Court
content: The government is against extending the creamy layer to SC and ST reservation benefits, emphasizing that the challenges these communities face are rooted in more than economic issues. Reservation serves to right historical wrongs and ensure equitable access. The Supreme Court has permitted states to categorize castes within SC groups, but only Parliament holds the power to amend the lists of SC and ST populations eligible for these allocations.

title: Rahul reaches out to Gen Z through Instagram, backs student protest in Jharkhand
content: Rahul Gandhi took to Instagram to voice his support for student protests, labeling the education system as deeply flawed and in need of urgent reform. His remarks were made following a meeting with NEET protesters who detailed their encounters with police brutality. The students bravely shared stories of discrimination they faced while advocating for their rights.

title: Opposition opposes FCRA bill, says minorities being targeted
content: Rahul Gandhi briefed opposition parties on discussions regarding the delimitation bill.  The opposition maintains its stand on women's reservation within the current Lok Sabha strength.  Discussions also covered the FCRA bill, with concerns raised about its impact on minorities.  Some members noted potential government removal of retrospective effect clauses.  Parliamentary functioning remains contingent on government statements regarding protests and donations.

title: BJP to Congress: Let House function, Amit Shah will come
content: The BJP has called out Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge for allegedly spreading misinformation. They assert that Home Minister Shah is present at Parliament House, but is unable to participate due to ongoing protests. Continued disruptions by the opposition hinder legislative work, yet Shah is ready to address their concerns directly. The BJP confirmed Shah is in his office daily, awaiting the resumption of parliamentary activities.

title: Land-grab case: Supeme Court grants interim bail to Abhishek's PA
content: In a significant move, the Supreme Court has granted interim bail for one week to Sumit Roy, who serves as the personal assistant to TMC general secretary Abhishek Banerjee. Roy is implicated in the Salboni land-grabbing case, which followed the arrest of former TMC MLA Sujoy Hazra. Notably, the court has stayed Roy's arrest until it reconvenes for the next hearing.

title: 3 rebel TMC MPs to meet Prime Minister over breakfast
content: A trio of dissenting Trinamool MPs is set to engage with Prime Minister Narendra Modi following their earlier discussions with Union Minister Amit Shah related to pressing concerns. Notably, these lawmakers have distanced themselves from two NDA meetings. Additionally, other NCPI representatives and Shiv Sena MPs are expected to join them for a breakfast meeting with the Prime Minister on Friday morning.

title: Priyanka Chopra joins Russell Crowe in Hollywood sci-fi action thriller 'Bluefly'
content: Priyanka Chopra Jonas has announced her next Hollywood venture, a sci-fi action thriller.  She will star opposite Russell Crowe in the film titled 'Bluefly'.  The movie's plot involves a deep Congo mission to recover a mysterious downed aircraft.  This project marks another significant international role for the acclaimed Indian actress.  'Bluefly' is scheduled for production and release in the future.

title: 15 Indian seafarers killed in West Asia and Black Sea conflicts: Regulator
content: Geopolitical conflicts in West Asia and the Black Sea have endangered Indian seafarers.  Fifteen Indian seafarers have died and two remain missing in recent months.  Drone and missile attacks have become rampant in the Black Sea region.  Piracy off Somalia and Houthi threats have also resurfaced significantly.  India's maritime regulator is enhancing safety measures and tracking seafarers' well-being.

title: Amid cyber threats, IT ministry asked to expedite hirings
content: The finance ministry has sanctioned more posts for CERT-In, yet the hiring remains underway. With rising cyber threats dominating discussions, a parliamentary committee is pressing for expedited recruitment. The IndiaAI Mission's fellowship program initially struggled to attract candidates. In response, MeitY is implementing outreach sessions and promotional campaigns to encourage more applicants. Additionally, final touches are being made to recruitment guidelines for several scientific roles ahead of future job advertisements.

title: SC says compulsory retirement not punitive, upholds CISF officer’s removal
content: The Supreme Court clarified that compulsory retirement is not a punishment for diminished performance, but rather a necessary step to uphold the standards of efficiency and discipline required. The court dismissed a plea from a CISF officer who disputed his removal after his performance had notably dropped from 'Good' to 'Average'. It emphasized the importance of consistent high performance among personnel in disciplined forces.

title: Wangchuk gives govt 1 month to drop cases, compensate for Leh protest firing
content: In a bold move, the Leh Apex Body has presented the Union government with a one-month ultimatum, calling for the withdrawal of allegations against protesters and support for the families affected by last year’s tragedies. The relatives of four deceased demonstrators are adamant about receiving justice and compensation. They have signaled potential protests if their requests are ignored, underscoring the urgent need for the Centre's attention to Ladakh's pressing concerns.

title: J&K Police file FIR over PDP’s Article 370 anniversary rally, party says ‘blatant misuse of power, authority’
content: The name of former J&K Chief Minister Mufti has been mentioned in the FIR for taking out a rally on August 4 and August 5 in the city, on the seventh anniversary of the abrogation of Article 370, “without prior police permission”

title: National Handloom Day: Inside the Bonda tribe’s enduring Ringa weaving tradition
content: On National Handloom Day, a look at how women of Odisha’s Bonda tribe continue to preserve the handwoven Ringa, a weave that defines their identity

title: The hands that are shaping Amaravati
content: As Andhra Pradesh’s greenfield capital takes shape, stories of migrant workers, women finding new livelihoods, and efforts to balance development with social and environmental concerns reveal the human side of building a new city. Their experiences shed a unique light on how an ambitious project is reshaping lives alongside the landscape of the capital region, writes P. Sujatha Varma

title: Karnataka’s rice bowl shows no signs of filling up
content: Deficit rain recorded in June and July because of El-Nino, impact of the West Asia war and some local factors in the rice growing areas have all pushed the price of various rice varieties, writes Rashmi Patil

title: In Telangana, property owners locked out of their own land
content: Several owners of legally purchased plots, houses and apartments across Telangana are finding themselves unable to sell, mortgage or transfer their properties after entire survey numbers containing prohibited categories such as Bhoodan, waqf, ceiling surplus and assigned lands were brought under the Section 22A prohibited list. But the Congress-led government says not one cent of land has been deliberately added to the list since it assumed office in December 2023. P. Laxma Reddy and M. Rajeev explore the ground situation

title: Bengal BJP fights against its ‘Trinamoolification’
content: Having coming to power in West Bengal earlier this year, the State unit of the BJP is facing a major political challenge, which party leaders are describing as its ‘Trinamoolification’. Implicit in this word is that several leaders from the Trinamool Congress are joining the party and being given key responsibilities, and that the BJP is embracing the very culture of the party it opposed and contested against, finds Shiv Sahay Singh

content: A New Mexico court has ordered Instagram and Facebook parent company Meta to pay $567 million to address harms to young people from its platforms in the second phase of a landmark trial the social media giant lost in March.

content: US President Donald Trump on Thursday told reporters that he believed the war with Iran would be over soon and said the armed forces were experiencing issues with supplies of some weapons.
